basis.governing_question: Should Quinta Azul enter the retail markets of Spain, France, Germany and Poland, and in which order?

phases.name: Research
phases.objective_one_line: Assess each retail market's attractiveness and Quinta Azul's ability to win there, and shortlist the markets for entry design.

gate.label: Findings sign-off
gate.decision: Which markets go forward into entry design, and which stop here?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define entry options and business cases per shortlisted market, and set the entry sequence and roadmap.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the go/no-go per country and the entry sequence?

workstreams.name: Market desk screen
workstreams.answers: Which of the four countries are attractive enough in retail olive oil to assess in full?
activities: Gather desk data on retail olive-oil demand per country
Compare the four markets on size and growth
Propose the markets to assess in full

workstreams.name: Market demand assessment
workstreams.answers: How large, how fast-growing and how attractive is each shortlisted country's retail olive-oil demand?
activities: Size demand and growth, two markets at a time
Analyze retail sales and price data per market
Interview consumers and buyers on purchase drivers

workstreams.name: Competition and access
workstreams.answers: Which competitors, retail channels and regulations shape Quinta Azul's access to each shortlisted country?
activities: Map competitors and retail channels in each market
Review the regulations that govern olive-oil sales
Interview retailers and distributors about supplier access

workstreams.name: Capability to win
workstreams.answers: Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in each shortlisted country?
activities: Review Quinta Azul's assets using operational data
Interview the people who produce and sell the oil
Assess gaps against what each market requires

workstreams.name: Entry options and cases
workstreams.answers: Which entry option and business case support a go or no-go in each shortlisted country?
activities: Compare entry options per market on agreed criteria
Build business cases, two markets at a time
Test case assumptions with buyers and Quinta Azul staff

workstreams.name: Entry sequence and roadmap
workstreams.answers: In what order, and on what roadmap, should Quinta Azul enter the countries that are a go?
activities: Compare entry order options across the countries
Draft the roadmap for the countries that are a go
Review the sequence with the CEO and Commercial Director

deliverables.name: Desk screen of the four markets and proposed shortlist
Interim demand findings for the first two markets
Retail demand assessment by shortlisted country
Competitor, channel and regulation review by country
Capability gap assessment of Quinta Azul's assets
Findings pack for the entry-design shortlist decision
Entry options compared per shortlisted country
Business case for each shortlisted country
Go/no-go and entry sequence pack with roadmap

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Start the work and agree the criteria
events.decision: Which criteria will shortlist the markets and decide each go or no-go?
agenda: Present the question on the four markets and the research phase
Discuss the data and people the market evidence work needs
Decide the criteria for shortlisting markets and for each go or no-go

events.label: Workshop: first findings
events.purpose: Test the shortlist against first findings
events.decision: Which of the other two markets should the demand assessment take up next?
agenda: Present the desk screen and the proposed shortlist
Review the interim demand findings for the first two markets
Decide which of the other two markets the demand work takes up next

events.label: Findings sign-off
events.purpose: Decide which markets go into entry design
events.decision: Which markets go forward into entry design, and which stop here?
agenda: Present the demand, competition and capability findings
Review the findings pack for the entry-design shortlist
Decide which markets go forward into entry design

events.label: Check-in: business cases
events.purpose: Review entry options and business cases
events.decision: Which entry option per country should the sequence and roadmap build on?
agenda: Present the entry options compared per shortlisted country
Review the business case for each shortlisted country
Discuss what the business cases mean for go or no-go per country

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Approve go/no-go and the entry sequence
events.decision: Approve the go/no-go per country and the entry sequence?
agenda: Present the go/no-go and entry sequence pack with roadmap
Review the entry options and business cases behind it
Decide the go/no-go per country and the entry sequence

architect_notes: Length is not given, so the 11 to 15 weeks are an estimate (work sizes at 11 to 17); confirm it before quoting.
Research and Design sit mid-estimate; slow buyer-interview access or client review rounds would push them to 10 and 7 weeks.
Assumes three of the four markets are assessed in full after the desk screen; assessing two would cut Research by 2 to 3 weeks.
A market dropped at the desk screen gets its no-go on desk evidence only; confirm that meets the go/no-go criterion.

sub_questions.question: How large and attractive is each country's retail market for Quinta Azul's olive oil?
Which competitors, retail channels and regulations shape Quinta Azul's access to each market?
Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in each market?
Which entry option and business case support a go or no-go for each of the four countries?
In what order, and with what roadmap, should Quinta Azul enter the countries that are a go?

drivers.evidence: retail markets of Spain, France, Germany and Poland

phases.name: Research

work.unit: Market assessed in full (demand, channels, competitors, regulation, buyer interviews)

phases.why: Four screened at once, three assessed in full two at a time; the desk screen before full work exceeds typical 4 to 8 weeks.

phases.name: Design

work.unit: Entry option and business case for one market
Entry sequence and roadmap across markets

phases.why: Three business cases built two at a time, then one sequence and roadmap; top of the range exceeds typical 3 to 6 weeks.

sizing.levers: Assessing two markets in full instead of three, or running all three at once, would shorten Research most.
